blocks.content: Rivers are the lifelines of India's agrarian economy, shaping its physical landscape, cultural heritage, and socioeconomic development.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Rivers are categorized into Major (>20,000 sq km catchment), Medium (2,000-20,000 sq km), and Minor (<2,000 sq km) basins.
Himalayan rivers are perennial and youthfully active, while Peninsular rivers are mature, seasonal, and rain-fed.
River systems act as the backbone of Indian agriculture, providing essential canal irrigation across alluvial plains.
Inland water transport, facilitated by designated National Waterways like NW-1 (Ganga), offers cost-effective freight transit.
Rivers generate substantial hydroelectric potential and sustain eco-sensitive riverine ecosystems and cultural heritage.
